demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Triggers.value: Talk about people loosing loved ones

Maladaptive Strategies.value: mentally rehearse worst case scenarios to feel prepared
Dates or anniversaries connected to the event
Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively

issues.item: Triggers: Animal Phobia: Talks or photos about snakes
issues.explanation: These trigger items are not clinically coherent with the indexed trauma of unexpected/traumatic death of a loved one. Snake-related and pregnancy/birth reminders imply trauma contexts unrelated to bereavement, and there is no supporting threat or memory content linking them to this loss.

issues.item: Triggers: Pregnancy/Birth Reminders: Pregnancy, childbirth, or babies in general
issues.explanation: Avoiding military/police uniforms or weapons similarly implies a trauma context involving violence, combat, or armed threat, which is unsupported by the stated trauma type and by the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Triggers: Pregnancy/Birth Reminders: Pregnancy, childbirth, or babies in general
issues.explanation: For an index trauma of unexpected/traumatic death of a loved one, pregnancy/birth reminders are hard to justify unless the death specifically involved childbirth or infant loss; nothing else in the profile supports that context. This makes the trigger clinically implausible relative to the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Uniform or Weapons: Military, police uniforms or weapons
issues.explanation: Avoiding military/police uniforms or weapons implies a trauma context involving combat, assault, or armed responders. That does not fit the rest of this bereavement-focused profile and is not supported by the other trigger, threat, or strategy items, so it appears incoherent with the trauma type and overall formulation.

vignette: Rohan's life was forever changed on a crisp autumn morning two years ago when his younger brother, Karan, suddenly passed away in a car accident. Rohan, then 37, was devastated by the loss of his closest sibling and confidant. As the anniversary of Karan's death approached, Rohan found himself increasingly anxious and withdrawn. He would often mentally rehearse worst-case scenarios to feel prepared for the impending doom he felt was lurking around every corner. This coping mechanism, which he had developed over time, helped him momentarily distract himself from the overwhelming grief that threatened to consume him. However, this strategy of worst-case rehearsal only served to heighten Rohan's sense of threat, as his mind would spiral into catastrophic thoughts about losing other loved ones or facing similar tragedies in the future. His body would react before his mind could even process these thoughts, leaving him on edge and easily startled. Irritability had become a hallmark of his behavior, with outbursts directed at his wife, Rhea, and colleagues becoming more frequent. He couldn't help but feel like he was walking on eggshells, waiting for the next shoe to drop. As anniversaries of Karan's death drew near, Rohan became increasingly avoidant of anything that reminded him of his loss. He stopped attending social gatherings or visiting places they used to frequent together, fearing it would trigger a flashback or an emotional breakdown. Even conversations about people losing loved ones made him uncomfortable, and he found himself changing the subject or excusing himself from discussions that veered too close to grief-related topics. Rohan's job as an interior designer began to suffer as well. His creative energy was stifled by his preoccupation with worst-case scenarios, making it difficult for him to focus on design projects. Rhea, who had been supportive throughout this ordeal, started noticing the toll Rohan's avoidance and irritability were taking on their relationship. She encouraged him to seek help, pointing out that his coping mechanisms were only perpetuating a cycle of fear and anxiety. Despite his efforts to push through, Rohan found himself increasingly isolated and withdrawn. His fear of confronting his grief had become paralyzing, making everyday tasks feel daunting. As the second anniversary of Karan's passing approached, Rohan realized he couldn't continue living in this state of hypervigilance. He knew it was time to confront his pain head-on, rather than letting it dictate his life. With a deep sense of trepidation and hope, Rohan made the decision to seek professional help, taking the first step towards breaking free from the grip of his trauma. Now, as he prepares for therapy, Rohan is most afraid that reliving his grief will be too much to bear, but also hopes to learn new ways to cope with his emotions, allowing him to reconnect with Rhea and rediscover his passion for design.
